exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Joining the Science Club
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lucy: Hi Tom, are you going to join the science club this year?
Tom: Yes, I really want to. I love asking questions about how things work.
Lucy: Me too. What kind of project do you hope to do?
Tom: I'd like to study how clean water can stop disease.
Lucy: That sounds useful. I want to build a small telescope and look at the stars.
Tom: Wow, that's a great idea. We could even share what we learn with the class.
Lucy: Exactly. The teacher says a real scientist always shares the results.
Tom: Then let's sign up right now before the club is full!

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 What Scientists Really Do
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Many people think scientists only mix liquids in a lab.
In fact, their work always begins with a question about the world.
They make a guess and then look for evidence to test it.
They take careful measurements and study the numbers.
Finally, they share their results so that everyone can benefit.
exercises.translation_cn: 许多人以为科学家只是在实验室里调配液体;其实他们的工作总是始于一个关于世界的问题;他们先做出猜想,再寻找证据去检验;他们仔细测量并研究数据;最后把成果分享出去,让所有人都能受益。

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 In the Laboratory
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: David: Maria, our first two results don't match at all. I feel frustrated.
Maria: Don't worry. When data look contradictory, we simply test again.
David: But we've already run the experiment three times.
Maria: Then let's calm down and check every measurement slowly.
David: You're right. Maybe one of the numbers was written down wrong.
Maria: Exactly. A real scientist has to be patient and careful.
David: I see. So one strange result is not the end of the world.
Maria: No. It's just a sign that we need to do some solid work.
exercises.translation_cn: 戴维说前两次结果完全不一致,感到沮丧;玛利亚说数据看似矛盾时,就再做一次;戴维说已经做了三次;玛利亚建议冷静下来逐项核对测量;戴维意识到可能有个数字记错了;玛利亚说真正的科学家必须耐心而细致;戴维明白一个奇怪的结果不是世界末日;玛利亚说那只是提醒他们要踏实工作。

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 The Story of Stephen Hawking
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Stephen Hawking was a gifted scientist who studied the universe.
He became famous while he was still a young student.
At a lecture, he stood up and found a mistake in the maths.
When the maths was corrected, the big bang theory was proven right.
Above all, he was brave and willing to admit his own faults.

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Advice on Doing Research
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Anna: I want to start a small research project, but I don't know how to begin.
Mr Lee: Start with a clear question that you really want to answer.
Anna: All right. What should I do after that?
Mr Lee: Make a guess, and then collect evidence to test it.
Anna: How do I know if my result is trustworthy?
Mr Lee: Repeat the test, and ask a friend to repeat it too.
Anna: That makes sense. So one result is never enough.
Mr Lee: Right. And remember to share what you find with others.
exercises.translation_cn: 安娜想做一个小研究项目却不知如何开始;李老师建议先提出一个真正想回答的清晰问题;然后做出猜想并收集证据去检验;安娜问如何判断结果是否可信;李老师说要重复实验,并请同学也重复一次;安娜明白一个结果远远不够;李老师叮嘱她要把发现分享给别人。

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 A Tip for Young Scientists
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is a simple tip for any young person who loves science.
Never be afraid to ask a question, even a strange one.
Every great discovery once began as a single curious question.
If your first idea is wrong, try again with fresh eyes.
A curious mind today can change the world tomorrow.
exercises.translation_cn: 给每一个热爱科学的年轻人一个小贴士:永远不要害怕提问,哪怕是个奇怪的问题;每一项伟大的发现都曾始于一个好奇的问题;如果第一个想法错了,就换个角度重新尝试;今天一颗好奇的心,明天能改变世界。
